author: Codex / comp07 independent architectural mass author
assumptions: Required programme and floor area are unknown; no scheme certifies programme compliance or targets maximum FAR.
The supplied reference asks for four visibly separate occupied blocks with differing orientations, not a single prism with superficial cuts.

Five storeys is the supplied parcel limit. The six propositions retain explicit height relationships while plan fitting remains available. Terrain, structure, cores, egress and parking remain unverified.

schemes.name: sangok_c07_four_rotated_occupied_blocks
schemes.secondary_language: Four distinct occupied blocks alternate orientation above one grounded block
schemes.formal_principle: Four substantial occupied blocks overlap vertically while their alternating orientations expose each level and address different directions.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Four readable blocks in a vertical rotated stack
schemes.reference_basis: Original interpretation of the user-supplied four-block mass study; no inferred room programme.

ops.why: The reference calls for discrete occupied masses rather than one sculpted envelope; place exactly one substantial block on each of four levels, with alternating 48-degree relative orientations and modest overlap-preserving displacement. This exposes four inhabited volumes and changing outlooks; transfer structure, vertical circulation and upper-level access remain unverified.

schemes.name: sangok_c07_offset_paired_bar_levels
schemes.secondary_language: Two grounded paired bars carry two offset upper bars
schemes.formal_principle: Two parallel grounded bars establish a shared passage, while two displaced upper bars make four occupied masses across two structural levels.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Paired lower and upper bars with a longitudinal gap
schemes.reference_basis: Original paired-building alternative to the compact four-block tower; programme allocation remains unknown.

ops.why: A compact vertical stack offers little independent ground address; instead use two grounded two-storey bars with a real separation and carry two shifted two-storey bars above them. Four masses now work as paired strata rather than four successive floors; passage usability, enclosed connections and cantilever reinforcement require verification.

schemes.name: sangok_c07_inhabited_bridge_between_piers
schemes.secondary_language: An occupied upper bridge joins two grounded room-depth piers
schemes.formal_principle: Two deep grounded volumes support a continuous occupied upper bridge, making the central ground opening the principal spatial event.
schemes.dominant_gesture: A substantial inhabited bridge over an open ground interval
schemes.reference_basis: Original alternative testing continuity above and permeability below; access permission and exact room functions remain unknown.

ops.why: Test whether the same unspecified building can keep its upper occupied volume continuous while releasing a meaningful central ground interval. Three storeys provide a bounded sectional budget; this is not a required-area assertion.

A central ground route conflicts with upper continuity; raise only the middle underside while leaving two broad piers grounded and an occupied upper band intact. The delivered section must show both piers, the opening and the bridge depth; this does not verify long-span engineering or circulation.

schemes.name: sangok_c07_grounded_wings_common_roof
schemes.secondary_language: Three grounded room volumes share a thin elevated roof plane
schemes.formal_principle: Three grounded volumes retain independent edges while one elevated roof plane binds the spaces between them into a sheltered collective interior.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Independent grounded wings beneath a common roof
schemes.reference_basis: Original distributed-building alternative; no landscape design, room schedule or roof engineering is claimed.

ops.why: A single deep building can hide the independence of its parts; distribute three substantial grounded volumes and connect their upper region with a common non-occupied roof plane, keeping intervening ground open. The roof is a unifying building element, not a landscaped podium; its bearing, span, drainage and sheltered routes remain design obligations.

schemes.name: sangok_c07_stepped_interlocking_sections
schemes.secondary_language: Three stepped occupied tiers are clasped by a transverse middle-level volume
schemes.formal_principle: Three unequal occupied tiers step toward one address, and a middle-level clasp gives the section a distinct transverse direction.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Asymmetric stepped tiers with a sectional interlock
schemes.reference_basis: Original sectional composition distinct from the rotating stack and paired bars; programme remains unspecified.

ops.why: Test a continuous occupied hierarchy with substantial retreating tiers rather than separate rotated blocks; keep one face aligned and let three unequal tiers expose usable stepped edges within a four-storey height budget. Floor division and terrace access remain unverified.

A uniform setback sequence alone lacks a second spatial direction; introduce two opposed, height-staggered clasp volumes on the middle tier. Their overlap makes a sectional relationship visible instead of adding a rooftop ornament; member sizes and occupiable headroom must be resolved.

schemes.name: sangok_c07_continuous_court_section
schemes.secondary_language: One continuous inhabited courtyard body changes height across its perimeter
schemes.formal_principle: A single courtyard body keeps one continuous spatial boundary while a low front and higher rear make its section differ from the assembled alternatives.
schemes.dominant_gesture: Continuous enclosure with one asymmetric sectional transition
schemes.reference_basis: Original continuous-volume control against the five assembled or bridged propositions; no required programme is supplied.

ops.why: Use one continuous building as a control against the other assembled propositions. Four storeys bound the highest edge without asserting an area target.

Continuity around a court conflicts with a uniformly tall edge; retain a full-height sky opening and change the occupied envelope from a two-storey front to a four-storey rear. The output must show actual continuous enclosure and a sectional transition, not planted open space; entrance cuts, rooms, daylight and structural design remain unknown.
